analyst.summary: VIP Industries just posted a Rs.338cr net loss for FY26 on revenue down 15%, with roughly Rs.130cr of that tied to a deliberate inventory clean-up by its new private-equity owner (Multiples Group took control from the Piramal family in mid-2025) - but even adjusting for that one-off, the core business is still losing money. The bigger issue is competitive: VIP's share of the organized luggage market has fallen from about 47% five years ago to roughly 29% today, while rival Safari Industries has overtaken it at ~32% share and is growing profitably. The balance sheet is stretched (debt nearly three times reserves) and next quarter's results (due by mid-August) are still pending. New management has guided to a revenue recovery in FY27, but volume is guided to grow faster than revenue, which itself signals continued discounting rather than a clean, margin-accretive turnaround. We rate this a Sell.
